text:
maria: Quick heads-up — did a short bring-up run comparing prefill+decode perf and $/1M tokens across H100 vs A100 for Llama-2-13B and GPT-J-6B (int8). Results are noisy but there are consistent patterns.

kevin: awesome, can you paste the summary numbers?

maria: copied condensed table below (run = single instance, 2048 context, batch=1 for latency; throughput measured via microbench for steady decode).
```
Model    | Region     | HW   | prefill_p50 | decode_p50(ms/token) | tok/sec | $/1M toks
Llama-2-13B | us-west1    | H100 | 280ms       | 18ms/token           | 2400    | $17.8
Llama-2-13B | us-central1 | A100 | 360ms       | 28ms/token           | 1600    | $22.4
GPT-J-6B    | us-west1    | H100 | 160ms       | 11ms/token           | 4200    | $12.2
GPT-J-6B    | us-central1 | A100 | 210ms       | 17ms/token           | 2600    | $15.6
Notes: int8 quant gave ~30% cost reduction, but decode latency increased ~4–6ms on A100. Kernel picks: on H100 the custom tensor-kernel (gpt_fast) outperformed aten paths; on A100 aten_gemm or cublasTNT better.
```

ajay: nice. Any sign that prefill dominates for short prompts?

maria: yes — for <300 tokens prefill is the biggest contributor. H100 prefill advantage stems from faster cross-layer attention kernels and better memcpy overlap. With caching enabled prefill can be amortized for multi-turns.

tara: how would this affect capacity planning for a dedicated pool? e.g., 10k qps of 1–2 token prompts vs chat workloads

maria: quick rule-of-thumb from these runs: provision based on worst-case decode p95 + prefill if you expect many single-shot short queries. Example: for Llama-2-13B on H100 target p95 latency ~600ms needs ~200 tokens/sec headroom per card (so ~12–14 concurrent single-shot streams). For throughput-heavy chat (longer tails) use batching + KV cache — that moves economics towards A100 if you can tolerate slightly higher latency but want lower $/token at scale.

kevin: any reproducible kernel config we should pin on deploys?

maria: for H100 pin kernel=gpt_fast + fp16-int8 quant profile_v2. For A100 pin aten_gemm and enable workspace tuning; also use the new kernel-fallback policy so we can route to aten if gpt_fast fails. Will push a config PR to infra tomorrow.

eval-bot: started eval run 1798504321-rlf-run to compute instruction-following regression after quant. Expecting results in ~4h.

ajay: thanks — can you add a small experiment to measure decode jitter (p50/p95/p99) across kernel choices? that p99 really matters for SLAs.

maria: on it, will run jitter sweep across regions and post charts. For now, don't change any production routing until I send the config PR + perf graphs. :thumbsup:
